issue: Does § 2254(e)(1)'s clear-and-convincing presumption of correctness provide the mechanism for proving that a state court's factual finding was unreasonable under § 2254(d)(2), or should the two provisions be synthesized differently?

sides.position: § 2254(e)(1) provides the mechanism for proving unreasonableness under § 2254(d)(2); the petitioner must rebut the presumption of correctness by clear and convincing evidence.
Other circuits synthesize § 2254(d)(2) and § 2254(e)(1) differently. The excerpt does not state this rule, and the cited concurrence only describes the split.
cases: Hayes v. Sec'y, Fla. Dep't of Corr., 10 F.4th 1203 (11th Cir. 2021) (Newsom, J., concurring)

this_court: § 2254(e)(1) provides the mechanism for proving unreasonableness under § 2254(d)(2)
quote: In our Circuit, we have decided that “§ 2254(e)(1) provides the mechanism for proving unreasonableness [under § 2254(d)(2)],” see Ben‐Yisrayl v. Buss, 540 F.3d 542, 549 (7th Cir. 2008), although other circuits have taken different approaches, see Hayes v. Sec’y, Fla. Dep’t of Corr., 10 F.4th 1203, 1223 (11th Cir. 2021) (Newsom, J., concurring) (describing the circuit split on how to synthesize § 2254(d)(2) and § 2254(e)(1)).
cite: Ricky Thurston v. Frank Vanihel, 39 F.4th 921 (7th Cir. 2022)
